Stage 2 retains all 23 documented components/150 EC and separates genuine open study from unknown required final-year study. Current primary module content and strengthened UCR challenges support a bounded negative conclusion; no complete cohort/final-work access certificate.

audience.programmeDescription: Cybersecurity & Cybercrime at Leiden combines computing, governance, law and criminology to study digital security and crime. Students examine how networked systems work, how attacks occur, who commits and experiences cybercrime, and how organisations and public institutions can respond. Research methods, academic skills and multidisciplinary projects connect these perspectives.
audience.comparisonExplanation: No close UCR comparison was found for the documented curriculum. UCR has genuine strengths in computing, law, misinformation, digital ethics and organizational study. Its strongest combinations do not sustain Leiden’s integrated study of cyber threats, crime, protection and response. The unpublished required third-year study remains separate from this academic judgment.

curriculum.limitation: The listed components total 150 EC: 120 EC of compulsory study in the first two years and 30 EC of third-year elective space. The remaining 30 EC of compulsory third-year study, including the final project, still require confirmation. This is an incomplete curriculum, not a certified 180-EC degree plan.

componentNotes.y1-skills-1: The skills labs develop academic and professional skills in small groups. Attendance and assessment requirements apply.
componentNotes.y1-project: A 10-EC multidisciplinary project on online deception and disinformation. Its credits are counted once within the first year.
componentNotes.y2-defence: Builds on the study of cyber attacks, moving from vulnerabilities to access controls, defensive measures and organisational security.
componentNotes.y2-project: A 10-EC multidisciplinary ransomware project, counted within the second year. Attendance and individual assessment requirements apply.
componentNotes.y3-open-elective-space: 30 EC for electives, a minor or approved study or internship options. Level, approval and non-overlap rules apply. Honours courses and specified overlapping minors and courses cannot be used here.

comparisonScope.label: No close UCR comparison
comparisonScope.assessed: The 23 documented components totaling 150 EC: 120 EC of first- and second-year compulsory study and 30 EC of genuine open study. The confirmed technical, criminological, legal, governance and integration teaching informs the judgment.
comparisonScope.excluded: The remaining 30 EC of required third-year study, individual final-project weight and assessment/access requirements, and full degree progression. The documented subset is not a certified complete 180-EC degree plan.

acceptance.targetContext: Ordinary Leiden BSc Cybersecurity & Cybercrime, 59348/1001O8924, dated 2026–2027 BA-BACC curriculum, no formal route. Supported 150 EC; full final-year curriculum/progression not certified.
acceptance.challengeMethod: Separately identified same-AI source-first pass against actual official/UCR evidence and exact finished fields; no independent human or separate-agent endorsement.

uncertainties.fact: The remaining 30 EC of required third-year units/individual weights and final-project entry/assessment are unpublished. Public material gives final article/poster format but not complete allocation.

adverseResolutions.resolution: The remaining study deepens technical security, cybercriminal inquiry, investigation or applied response.
adverseResolutions.effectOnClaim: Do not assume any such unit or weight. Known first-two-year cyber inquiry already establishes the taught subject-specific progression missing from the strongest UCR combinations. Additional specialist teaching cannot remove that known shortfall.

adverseResolutions.resolution: The remaining study emphasizes general governance, organizations, ethics or accessible interdisciplinary research and skills.
adverseResolutions.effectOnClaim: Grant those stronger UCR connections fully; the confirmed attack/defence, offending/victimology, digital investigation, incident response and ransomware integration remain part of the assessed core. Unknown final study cannot erase them. A positive core claim cannot silently omit known defining teaching.

uncertainties.fact: Fresh full OER allocation/final-work text could not be retrieved beyond current version header. Exact same-year formal findings actually inspected 13 November remain retained with version; no fresh full-body claim. Full progression/access is uncertified.

adverseResolutions.resolution: A current formal clarification changes final-work credit, access, assessment, choice restrictions or third-year progression.
adverseResolutions.effectOnClaim: Preserve the known final article/poster format without inventing weight or UCR equivalence. Reconcile any new material evidence in a separately authorized follow-up. The present bounded negative relies on independently current confirmed first-two-year academic substance, not a formal-access, language, licence or exact-format veto.
